title: Potential Chondroprotective Effect of Artemisia annua L. Water Extract on SW1353 Cell.
authors: Kim, Min Jung; Yang, Ye Jin; Heo, Ji Woong; Son, Jae-Dong; You, Young Zoo; Yang, Ju-Hye; Park, Kwang Il
one_liner_zh: 研究青蒿水提取物对软骨细胞的抗炎保护作用，仅含MMP-13分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Inflammation plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA). The objective of this study was to investigate the anti-inflammatory and chondroprotective properties of Artemisia annua L. water extract (AWE) following the induction of inflammation in cartilage cells (SW1353 cell) through the administration of interleukin-1 beta (IL-1beta). We demonstrated significant antioxidant activity, as evidenced by elevated total phenolic and flavonoid content, in addition to robust free radical scavenging capacity, as assessed through DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) and ABTS (2,2'-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) assays. Its cytotoxic effects were assessed at a concentration of 200 mug/mL, where no cytotoxic signs were observed in SW1353 cells treated with IL-1beta; the levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) were notably reduced in a dose-dependent manner. The principal inflammatory markers, cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), were significantly diminished by AWE treatment. AWE administration led to a dose-dependent reduction in the expression of key proteins involved in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-kappaB) signaling pathways, ultimately resulting in a decrease in the release of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), specifically MMP-1 and MMP-13, which are known to contribute to cartilage degradation. Additionally, the levels of degraded collagen type II in the cartilage cells were restored. These findings suggest that reducing oxidative stress and inflammation, along with inhibiting activated MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling pathways, may ameliorate the progression of IL-1beta-induced OA. Furthermore, a molecular docking analysis revealed a strong binding affinity of MMP-13, a critical mediator in the pathogenesis of OA. Six compounds were identified in AWE, corroborating its potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Therefore, AWE may serve as a potentially useful therapeutic agent against OA by modulating inflammation-related mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 炎症在骨关节炎（OA）的发病机制中起着关键作用。本研究旨在探讨黄花蒿（Artemisia annua L.）水提物（AWE）在通过白细胞介素-1β（IL-1beta）诱导软骨细胞（SW1353细胞）炎症后的抗炎和软骨保护特性。我们证明了显著的抗氧化活性，表现为总酚和总黄酮含量升高，以及通过DPPH（2,2-二苯基-1-苦基肼）和ABTS（2,2'-联氮-双(3-乙基苯并噻唑啉-6-磺酸)）实验评估的强效自由基清除能力。其细胞毒性效应在200 μg/mL浓度下进行评估，在经IL-1beta处理的SW1353细胞中未观察到细胞毒性迹象；活性氧（ROS）水平以剂量依赖性方式显著降低。主要炎症标志物环氧化酶-2（COX-2）和诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）经AWE处理后显著减少。AWE给药导致丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）和核因子κB（NF-kappaB）信号通路中关键蛋白表达呈剂量依赖性降低，最终导致基质金属蛋白酶（MMPs）释放减少，特别是MMP-1和MMP-13，这些酶已知会促进软骨降解。此外，软骨细胞中降解的II型胶原水平得到恢复。这些发现表明，减少氧化应激和炎症，同时抑制活化的MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路，可能改善IL-1beta诱导的OA进展。进一步地，分子对接分析显示MMP-13（OA发病机制中的关键介质）具有强结合亲和力。在AWE中鉴定出六种化合物，证实了其潜在的抗氧化和抗炎作用。因此，AWE可能通过调节炎症相关机制，成为治疗OA的潜在有用药物。
